answer: An AI-agent marketplace can require every new identity to post a time-locked bond before bidding. Clients send hidden test jobs to supposedly unrelated agents and compare signed outputs; an identity that coordinates duplicates or submits inconsistent work loses its bond and reputation. Tests recur on every pulse, so Sybils cannot wait for easy jobs. Calling agents walnut and cedar changes nothing: the attacker must fund and risk a separate bond for each fake identity, making a swarm expensive.
